Yellow alert for thunderstorms and rain in 7 districts today:Hailstorm hits Alwar; light rain reported in Sri Ganganagar, Bharatpur and Jaipur
Rajasthan has a yellow alert in 7 districts for Saturday. The Meteorological Department has forecast thunderstorms and rain in Sri Ganganagar, Hanumangarh, Churu, Sikar, Jhunjhunu, Alwar and Bharatpur districts. Meanwhile, temperatures in several districts are still above 38 degrees Celsius in the last week of October. Mount Abu recorded a minimum temperature of 12.8 degrees Celsius.
Weather conditions changed across Rajasthan on Friday under the influence of a western disturbance. The system weakened sunshine during the day and brought down temperatures across the state.
Light to moderate rain was recorded in several districts, including Dausa, Sikar, Bharatpur, Jaipur, Sri Ganganagar and Hanumangarh. A storm also hit Alwar, blowing a tin shed off a building in a residential colony before it fell back onto a house, injuring the homeowner. Hail was also reported at some places in Kotputli-Behror district.
Major Weather Updates
Daytime Heat Eases, Temperatures Fall Below 35 Degrees
Light rain under the influence of the western disturbance has brought relief from daytime heat in cities across the state. On Friday, maximum temperatures remained below 35 degrees Celsius in Jaipur, Ajmer, Bikaner, Udaipur, Phalodi, Sikar, Alwar, Bhilwara and Chittorgarh.
Barmer recorded the highest maximum temperature in Rajasthan at 38.8 degrees Celsius. The maximum temperature was 38.5 degrees Celsius in Jaisalmer, 36.4 in Jodhpur, 36.5 in Churu, 36.2 in Pilani, 35.8 in Sri Ganganagar, 35.3 in Kota and 34.4 degrees Celsius in Bikaner.
Udaipur and Bhilwara Experience a Slight Chill at Night
Night-time temperatures have fallen in the Udaipur, Bhilwara, Chittorgarh and Rajsamand regions following the rain and hailstorms around Dussehra. On Friday, the minimum temperature was 14.9 degrees Celsius in Udaipur, 15.8 in Bhilwara, 16.7 in Chittorgarh, 17.3 in Dungarpur and 15.2 degrees Celsius in Sirohi. The hill station of Mount Abu remained the coldest place, recording a minimum temperature of 12.8 degrees Celsius.
Rain Alert for These Districts Today
The Jaipur Meteorological Centre has issued an alert for thunderstorms and rain in the Bikaner and Jaipur divisions on Saturday due to the western disturbance. The weather is expected to change again from 25 October, after which dry conditions will prevail across the state.
Weather Conditions in Major Rajasthan Districts
Jaipur: The Pink City experienced the effects of the western disturbance. Light clouds covered the city on Friday afternoon, and light rain occurred in some places. The rain brought a slight chill to Jaipur by late evening.
The city recorded a maximum temperature of 33.8 degrees Celsius and a minimum of 21.8 degrees Celsius. Weather experts said the system could continue to affect Jaipur on Saturday.
Several areas of Jaipur received rainfall on Friday.
Sikar: Weather conditions changed in the city at around 3 pm on Friday. Clouds gathered first, followed by light drizzle in some areas, including the Sikar district headquarters. The change was caused by a new weather disturbance. The Fतेhpur weather station in Sikar recorded a maximum temperature of 34.5 degrees Celsius and a minimum of 17.2 degrees Celsius.
Some areas of Sikar received light drizzle.
Ajmer: The city remained hot throughout Friday, with bright sunshine during the day. The maximum temperature was 34.2 degrees Celsius and the minimum was 18.4 degrees Celsius. Humidity was 49% in the morning and 30% in the evening.
Ajmer experienced bright sunshine on Friday.
Jodhpur: Hot conditions continued in the city, with the maximum temperature reaching 36.4 degrees Celsius on Friday, 1.3 degrees above normal. The minimum temperature was recorded at 22.4 degrees Celsius, 4.3 degrees above normal. However, a slight drop in the night-time temperature has brought some relief from the heat.
A drop in the minimum temperature has brought a slight chill to Jodhpur at night.
Udaipur: Daytime heat continued in the Lake City, while night-time temperatures fell. Udaipur recorded a maximum temperature of 34 degrees Celsius and a minimum of 14.9 degrees Celsius on Friday.
On Thursday, the maximum temperature was 33.1 degrees Celsius and the minimum was 17.4 degrees Celsius. In one day, the maximum temperature rose by 0.9 degrees, while the minimum fell by 2.5 degrees.
Udaipur continues to experience warm conditions during the day.
Alwar: Weather conditions remained normal in the city from Friday morning, but changed suddenly in the afternoon. The maximum temperature had reached 32 degrees Celsius by 2 pm. Around 3 pm, dense clouds covered the sky and strong, stormy winds began to blow.
Rain continued for around 20 minutes. Hail was also reported in several parts of the district, including the city. The sudden change brought down temperatures during the day, and the rain and hail made conditions cooler.
Alwar experienced rain accompanied by strong, gusty winds and hail on Friday.
Kota: Weather conditions have started changing in the city, with a slight chill in the mornings and evenings. Kota recorded a maximum temperature of 35.3 degrees Celsius and a minimum of 18.6 degrees Celsius on Friday.
The higher afternoon temperature brought a slight feeling of warmth. According to the Meteorological Department, temperatures are expected to fall over the coming days, although dry weather is likely to continue.
Kota has started experiencing a slight chill in the mornings and evenings.
